tools.name: list_processes
tools.title: List process types (request types)
tools.description: Lists the enabled eXo Processes types (a.k.a. request types) the current user can see, or only those of one space with 'space_id' (in a run limited to a space, that space), e.g. 'Leave request', 'Expense report', 'IT support'. Use this to discover what the user can request and to get the process id ('id' in the result) to pass to submit_work_request. Each result also exposes 'projectId' (the underlying Task/Kanban project) and 'canManageRequests' (true when the user can see that process's pending requests, i.e. the process has a space and the user is a member of it or a platform administrator).

space_id.description: Optional. The id of a space: lists only the processes of that space. Without it, every process the user can see is listed.

tools.name: get_my_requests
tools.title: List my work requests
tools.description: Lists the current user's OWN work requests (the requests they submitted through a process), most recent first. Optionally filter by the column of the process's task board the request sits in. Each result tells 'completed' (closed: decided or canceled) from a pending request, 'canceled' when the user canceled it, and 'archived' when the user archived it. The 'id' of each result is the request id to pass to get_request_details or cancel_work_request.

status.description: Optional filter: the name of a column of the process's task board, which the board's owners name freely. Omit to list requests in every column.

tools.name: get_request_details
tools.title: Get a work request's details
tools.description: Retrieves the full details (title, description, status, completion, dates) of one of the current user's own work requests by its id. Call get_my_requests first to get the request_id.

request_id.description: The id of one of the current user's requests (the 'id' from get_my_requests).

tools.name: submit_work_request
tools.title: Submit a new work request
tools.description: Submits a new work request under a process type, on behalf of the current user. The request is created in the first column of the process's task board, and the platform names it '<process> - <yyyy/MM/dd> - <requester>'. Get 'process_id' from list_processes. A process with documents to fill is not submitted here: its requester fills them in the Process app, and this tool refuses it with processes.request.documentToFill, creating nothing. Prepare what you can for it (the description, the form values), then give the user the process's 'requestUrl' from list_processes to finish and submit there. A request may carry forms: the process's own and those of its board. Before submitting, read them: get_form_places with the place {kind 'task', place_type 'processes.process', place_id the process id} lists every form the request carries, then get_form with each form_id, place_type 'processes.process' and place_id the process id gives its fields. Send their values in 'form_values', filling every required field of every form, and put any other details the approver needs into the 'description'. A refusal names a code, followed by ':' and the field's form id and ':' and its key when it is about one field (such as forms.value.required:<formId>:<key>), or ':' and the key alone: fix that field of that form and submit again. In a call limited to a space, 'form_values' is refused.

process_id.description: The id of the process type to request (the 'id' from list_processes). The process must be enabled.

title.description: Optional. A short title of your own, e.g. 'Summer holidays', added after the name the platform gives the request: '<process> - <yyyy/MM/dd> - <requester> - <title>'. The whole name is cut to 250 characters, so a long title is shortened.

description.description: Optional free-text description / details of the request for the approver.

form_values.description: Optional. The values of the request's forms: form id (as a string key) -> field key -> array of values, such as {"12": {"amount": [150], "reason": ["Training"]}}. Each value is written as get_form describes its field's type, and a field with one value still takes an array. Never send null.

tools.name: cancel_work_request
tools.title: Cancel a work request
tools.description: Cancels one of the current user's own requests: closes it as canceled, leaving it in its column, and notifies the process's managers. Only the request's creator can cancel it, and only while it is pending: a request already closed (decided) is refused, one already canceled is returned as it is. Call get_my_requests first to get the request_id.

request_id.description: The id of the current user's request to cancel (the 'id' from get_my_requests).

tools.name: get_pending_approvals
tools.title: List pending requests I can see
tools.description: Lists the requests still pending a decision in the enabled processes whose space the current user is a member of, or, for a platform administrator, in every enabled process that has a space. A request is pending while its task is not completed, whatever column of the board it sits in ('status' names that column). It reads at most 200 processes and 100 requests. To respond to one, use the eXo Task tools on the returned 'taskId': call update_task_status to move it to the board's column that words the outcome, complete_task to close it as decided, and add_task_comment to leave a note. Returns an empty list when the user is neither a member of a process space nor a platform administrator, or has nothing pending.
